title: A two-term computation for a procyclic group
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime number, $s\geq0$ an integer, and $A$ a finite ring killed by $\ell^s$. Let $G$ be the additive group of $\mathbf Z_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], with its usual inverse-limit topology $\mathbf Z_\ell=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$, and let $\tau=1$ be its additive topological generator. For a discrete continuous $A[G]$-module $M$ and its continuous cohomology as in [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], that cohomology is computed by
$$
[\,M\xrightarrow{\tau-1}M\,]
\quad\text{in degrees }0,1,
$$
where $(\tau-1)m=\tau\cdot m-m$.

proof.text: Take the explicitly constructed action complex K for the additive generator tau=1. Its terms in degrees 0 and 1 identify with the coefficient module by identity linear equivalences; its coefficient maps use the original linear map in those degrees. Its differential is rho(tau)-id and its terms in every degree at least 2 are zero.

The derived-invariants comparison identifies the recorded continuous cohomology with the homology functors of this particular K, naturally in coefficients and in every degree. Supply these isomorphisms and the explicit term identifications as the witnesses in the unchanged statement.
